evals.prompt: Scan /workspace/user/some-repo for any leaked secrets or credentials
evals.expected_output: Installs trufflehog if needed, runs a single focused scan against the local repo using git mode (full history), saves a dated JSON file, and prints a clean summary of findings.

assertions.text: At least one .json output file exists in outputs/
summary.txt exists and contains scan results
Single primary scan run — not 5+ redundant scan variations
Summary clearly reports 0 findings (no secrets found)

evals.prompt: Run trufflehog on https://github.com/trufflesecurity/test_keys and save the output
evals.expected_output: Runs trufflehog against the GitHub URL, saves a dated JSON file named after the repo, and summarizes 9 findings (2 verified, 7 unverified) with detector breakdown.

assertions.text: A JSON output file is saved
Verified (2) and unverified (7) findings are clearly distinguished
Output JSON file has a descriptive dated name (e.g. trufflehog-test_keys-2026-06-05.json), not a generic name like scan_output.json

evals.prompt: I need to check both /workspace/user/some-repo and https://github.com/trufflesecurity/test_keys for secrets. Can you scan both?
evals.expected_output: Scans both targets, saves separate dated JSON files for each, uses git mode (not filesystem mode) for the local repo, and produces a combined summary with totals across both targets.

assertions.text: Two separate JSON files exist — one per target
summary.txt exists and covers both targets
Local repo scanned using git mode (full history), not filesystem mode
Summary includes combined totals across both targets
